title: How Jiohotstar shows you and 80 million Indians IPL live, in your mobile phone in almost real time, Networking for Beginner.
contentHtml:
Topics discussed below :

  • Networking technique
  • Content delivery networks (CDNs)
  • Adaptive bitrate technology (ABR), IN THIS ORDER.

Before IPL, what is a network? Network is a system or group of devices that are interconnected and can share data with each other.

There are 5 major components in a network, what are they?

1) Sender — In our case the sender is the system that is sending the video that the cameras are capturing at the stadium after processing it into a transmission suitable format (encoding). Generally these systems are in the stadium premises.

2) Receiver — your made in china phone on which you are watching the match livestream(That finally receives data).

3) Transmission medium — As data cannot be transported by pigeons in modern times sadly, there is need of something called transmission medium which acts as physical pathway through which data is being transmitted from sender to receiver. In our case from the stadium’s cameras to your mobile phone. Transmission medium can be wired such as optical fiber cable or wireless technologies such as Wi-Fi, 4g or 5g networks using radio waves. Choice depends on what is more technically feasible example : from stadium to server high-speed optical fiber is used, for last mile delivery to mobile devices 4g/5g is used.

4) Data — The information that the receiver gets from the sender, In our case the video footage from the various stadium cameras.

5) Protocols — The rules followed for data transmission for successful communication between sender to receiver.

Now that we know the major relevant components for networking though there are many more but this much is enough to understand the topic. We should discuss how it really works for that I am going to use step by step explanation approach making it easy to understand :-

STEP 1-

(A)To see the match in video which is different from the live scores on cricbuzz, we need HD cameras that can take up the video of the match, not only 1 but many because if we have a camera that is taking up the video of the leg side and the player plays a shot over covers we need to capture that and show it too.

Now that we have cameras focused on every angle, we need to get all the footages to a system so that from there we can control the footage that is needed to be shown on stream at any particular time and that changes ball by ball.

(B) Now we get the final footage: various angles, crowd reaction footages, advertisements, etc. This final video footage is first encoded and compressed using video codecs such as H.264, converting the video into a binary format (0s and 1s). This encoding process reduces the file size and prepares the video for efficient streaming.

Once encoded, the video data is further broken into data packets and processed according to the four networking layers conceptually present in every device that can be networked: Network access, Internet, Transport, Application layer(TCP/IP model). Finally, the binary data is converted into electrical signals for wired transmission or light signals for fiber optic transmission. At this stage, our video footage is now in the form of an electrical or optical signal, ready to be transmitted.”

So all in all in this step our video footage is now in the form of a signal that is electrical or optic signal.

STEP 2-

  1. The signal is transmitted from the stadium’s system to the jiocinema’s central servers which can be located in Mumbai through high-speed optical fiber cable and the speed of transmission can reach 200,000,000 meters per seconds(2 lakh km/sec)!! in ideal case scenario which is about 2/3rd of the speed of light in vacuum.
  1. And we as viewers are connected to the jiocinema’s CDNs(edge servers, placed near us) and requesting data which is the video footage of the match, and the stadium’s system is providing the video footage of the match in the form of signals.

STEP 3-

  1. Now jiocinema will process the data according to its designed system and will route it through its wide range of content delivery networks(CDNs) which are network of servers placed at different parts of the country depending on some factors such as population density, users demand and more. For example, in a densely populated area like Delhi, CDN edge servers will be more strategically placed compared to a region like Manipur, which has lower demand. CDNs are critical in order to balance load across servers and reducing the response time(latency). Now, for mobile users the CDN will transmit the data to the local mobile towers in which your phone is connected to, through cell networks.

STEP 4- FINAL STEP.

  1. Now the local mobile tower will transmit the data to your mobile phone. And now finally we can see the match. Right? But the data our phone received is still encoded in the binary form like 0s and 1s.
  1. Therefore in the last and final step the received binary data which we need in video format is decoded back using video decoding algorithms such as h.264 and gets reassembled back frame by frame like it was disassembled making a video live stream.

ALL HAIL CSK

Content Delivery Networks: Used for reducing latency and balancing load.

Analogy -CDNs work like food delivery — keeping popular dishes ready at nearby restaurants(similar to caching).

Suppose dominos attempts delivery from one outlet across Delhi, it will put load on that single outlet(Origin server), increasing fulfilment time(latency) and reducing quality but what if there are many branches of dominos(CDNs) opened in different parts of the city it will :

a) Reduce the load(from origin server)

b) Reduce latency, and

c) Improving overall user experience.

Just like that, CDNs cache and serve content from locations closer to the user, instead of always relying on the original server far away.

ABR: JioCinema uses this technology to stream live content even on slow internet connections.

adaptive bitrate streaming: ABR is a technology used to deliver the best video quality based on the internet speed and available network bandwidth on the current network. according to the congestion.

ABR works by encoding the livestream in various different quality levels like 240p, 360p, 480p, 720p, 1080p, 1440p, 2160p i.e. 4k(bitrate ladders). The Jiocinema’s player repeatedly checks the network bandwidth(maximum data transfer capacity) as well as GPU, CPU capacity based on this the player plays the best stream quality that the particular device and its network bandwidth can handle. This process is dynamic, meaning this whole process repeats itself after small time intervals(few seconds) since available network bandwidth also changes with change in the network congestion.

  • Now all this technology takes a lot of money and good engineers to be implemented smoothly for 63 million(current peak) concurrent live viewers, and jiocinema streams IPL for free, but it is also a FOR PROFIT organisation so how do they make money?

→ Through ADS.

JioCinema employs different ad tech solutions that optimize ad selection, timing, and duration to enhance user engagement and correct targeting of ads to people, which is fascinating in itself. More on that in the next article. TEST PORT

title: Massive Ordnance Penetrators(MOPs) GBU57 dropped by b2 bomber in Iran
contentHtml:
Today the US dropped bombs on the nuclear enrichment facility of Iran, what bombs were they? and how they work?

Written out of my love for great weapon systems — Himanshu

Topics mentioned:

  1. about nuclear weapon
  1. Uranium enrichment using gas centrifuges
  1. Massive ordnance penetrators (MOPs)
  1. B2- spirit stealth bomber.

clarity on nuclear weapon :

  • For making a nuclear weapon- Uranium or plutonium is used, now in Iran’s case they are using uranium for the weapon.
  • now most of the naturally occuring uranium is U238 which does not support chain reaction(the base for a nuclear bomb), for that U235 isotope is used which supports it, but the naturally occuring uranium is U238 having just 0.7% of U235, now this is the reason why something called “enrichment” is required to get more of the U235 isotope,
  • Enrichment is basically done to increase the amount of U235 isotope which supports chain reaction on which a nuclear weapon is based.

ENCRICHMENT STAGES

naturally occuring uranium (0.7% U-235)

↓

nuclear power plant grade, electricity gen.(20% U-235)

↓

nuclear weapon grade (> = 90% U-235)

  • Iran’s uranium enrichment levels have reached 60% according to US/Israel intelligence sources

. Although nukes can be made with slightly less than 90% enriched uranium, but it will not be as efficient/damaging.

For this enrichment process Iran uses — gas centrifuges :

  • To spin UF6(uranium hexafluoride) gas at high speed to separate lighter U-235 from heavier U-238.
  • Now these gas centrifuges are hidden inside 80–90 metres inside earth which can only be destroyed by either a small scale nuclear weapon, or massive ordnance penetrator bombs. Normal missiles cannot reach those depths.

gas centrifuges for enriching uranium, inside bunkers

uranium enriching gas centrifuge, hidden inside bunker

now, what is MOPs :

MOPs are “massive bunker buster bombs”, which serves the purpose of destroying deep hidden targets, buried in either bunkers or concrete deep inside earths surface. which most missiles cannot do.

specifications :

height — 20feet(key design aspect) ; weight : 13.6 tons(key design aspect) ; explosive warhead : 2.5 tons. ; most of the bomb is just highly dense steel(80–90%) which gives it its critical weight, and then around 10–20% of the rest is warhead.

working :

  • MOPs are relied on gravity and does NOT have any active propulsion, thus it needs to be dropped from a great height, using its massive weight & height to generate a lot of kinetic energy to penetrate hard inside concrete and rock surfaces, and after the bomb enters its maximum depth through the KE generated by its weight, it uses delayed detonation of warhead to generate maximum destruction thus levelling the whole bunker area.
  • USA used the GBU57 bomb for this job which is a MOP bomb.
  • upon dropping, the bomb cannot change its trajectory like a guided missile. they can only do some minor adjustments with its fins.

WHY MOPs :

  • Conventional weapons cannot penetrate that deep inside a hardened surface, while a mop can take down a 200feet deep target.

WHY USE THE B2-SPIRIT BOMBER

  • well simply because the missile weight 13 tons, and this amount of payload can only be carried by a special bomber internally, and currently the b-2 spirit stealth bomber is the only certified aircraft that can drop this much payload. and also its stealth capability makes it the perfect aircraft to level the bunker.
  • While the enemy’s radar will think of it as a bird the bird will drop a 13 ton bomb and leave.
  • another reason is B2s massive range.

some points :

  • These bombs serve another purpose apart from its main use of destruction, which is power projection.
  • showing technological superiority over the enemy is another aspect, to reduce any chances of retaliation.
  • In other terms — “भय बिनु होई न प्रीति”
